provider_if_inherited: Project management SaaS vendor; accounting SaaS vendor; email provider
implementation_statement: The SaaS vendors provide account functions; the owner creates and removes every account. Gaps: 9 subcontractor portal accounts from jobs closed in 2025 were still active; the bookkeeper uses the owner's accounting login; the laptop has one login shared with family. Owner removes portal users at each job closeout and creates a separate bookkeeper account by 2026-09-30.
evidence: SYS-01 user list export 2026-07-14; accounting user settings; laptop account settings

implementation_statement: SYS-01 enforces the permission template the owner assigns. Gap: the default subcontractor template shows the whole project folder, including other subcontractors' pricing and the full FC-1 drawing set. Owner sets a trade-only template for FC-1 by 2026-09-30. Laptop family use moves to separate standard accounts (AC-2).

No list of approved external systems existed. FCI reached a personal consumer cloud photo account, free file-transfer links, and the AI bid assistant. POL-01 section 8 (adopted 2026-08-31) lists the only approved places for FCI; photo sync for the work album is turned off and FC-1 uploads to the AI tool are stopped by 2026-09-30.
evidence: P07 AC-20 results; AI tool settings

implementation_statement: Only the owner posts to the company website and social media page. An April 2026 jobsite photo showed an FC-1 floor plan and was removed 2026-07-15. POL-01 9.4 now requires a check before posting any photo from a federal job.
evidence: Social media history; removed post screenshot

implementation_statement: No security training. The owner completes a free basic cybersecurity course for small businesses and a payment fraud module by 2026-11-30, and repeats a refresher each year.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody reviews email sign-in history, mailbox forwarding rules, or SYS-01 user activity. From 2026-10, the owner checks all three on the first business day of each month and before each pay app is sent, and records the check.

The first inventory of SaaS accounts, devices, and network equipment was written for this plan (section 9). Gap: it did not record manufacturers until the Section 889 inquiry found the covered hotspot on 2026-07-16. The inventory now records the manufacturer of every network device and is checked before any purchase.
The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: no standby supervision agreement, sealed recovery codes, or second sign-in method yet (due 2026-12-31).
regulatory_driver: Business need (P05); no FAR contingency requirement

provider_if_inherited: Project management SaaS vendor; email provider; accounting SaaS vendor
implementation_statement: The SaaS vendors back up their platforms (SYS-01 RPO 1 hour per its SOC 2 system description). Owner responsibility: laptop files (estimates, scanned lien waivers, W-9s) have no backup and there is no independent export of SYS-01 project records. Owner turns on file sync with version history for the laptop work folder and takes a quarterly SYS-01 export by 2026-10-31.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report (P09); laptop storage review
regulatory_driver: Business need (P05); FAR 52.222-8(a) payroll records kept 3 years

implementation_statement: The owner has a unique account on every service. Gaps: the bookkeeper uses the owner's accounting credentials and family members use the owner's laptop login, so actions cannot be tied to one person.

provider_if_inherited: SaaS vendors; bank; government sign-in service
implementation_statement: Every owner account is an administrator account. MFA is enforced by the bank (app approval) and the government sign-in service, and the email account uses text-message codes. Gap: SYS-01 and SYS-02 administrator sign-ins use a password only. Owner turns on app-based MFA for both by 2026-09-15 and adds a security key to email by 2026-10-31. FAR 52.204-21 does not require MFA; this addresses business email compromise (P01 R-001).
evidence: Account security pages; P07 sign-in tests

implementation_statement: The 23 external portal users in SYS-01 sign in with a password only. The vendor can require MFA for all users; the owner turns it on by 2026-09-30 and tells subcontractors in advance.

Passwords are owner-chosen with some reuse and no password manager. P07 found the home router still on its default administrator password with remote administration on (fixed 2026-07-21). Gaps: shared accounting password; no rule for changing passwords after a device or person change. Password manager and unique passphrases by 2026-09-15.

The business email compromise runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-08-31 with a notification matrix. Gap: contacts not yet verified and printed, and the runbook has not been walked through (due 2026-09-30).

No wipe procedure or records. The February 2026 laptop is in a drawer unwiped; the 2025 phone was traded in with no record. POL-01 8.6 sets the method (encrypted, then factory reset, or certified destruction) and a disposal log; the old laptop is wiped and kept as a spare by 2026-09-30.

Home office door has no lock; family and guests pass through. Plan sets ride in the truck cab. The storage unit has a gated code and the owner's padlock; a spare padlock key lent to a subcontractor in 2025 was never returned. Owner installs a keyed lock on the office door, keeps plan sets out of sight in a locked truck box, rekeys the storage unit, and keeps a key list by 2026-10-31.
First risk assessment completed 2026-07-17 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed every July and after a new system, a new federal contract, or an incident (POL-01 4.3).

The project management vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report was reviewed on 2026-07-16 (P09). Gaps: no review of the email, accounting, or AI vendors' terms; the AI tool's standard terms allowed use of uploads to improve the service; the bookkeeper's engagement letter has no confidentiality or security terms.
evidence: Vendor list; P09 vendor review; AI terms of service

implementation_statement: The laptop host firewall is on and SaaS traffic uses TLS. Gaps: the home router was unmanaged (default password and remote administration found 2026-07-21, fixed that day) with family and smart-home devices on the same network; the covered hotspot was used until 2026-07-16. Owner creates a separate work network on the router (guest network for family and smart-home devices) by 2026-09-30. No publicly accessible components are inside the boundary, so 52.204-21(b)(1)(xi) is not applicable.

Laptop full-disk encryption is on with the recovery key stored in the owner's account and on paper in the home office safe; the phone is encrypted by its passcode. SaaS vendors encrypt stored data (inherited). Not a FAR requirement; it keeps a lost device from becoming a data loss.
evidence: Encryption status screens (P07); vendor SOC 2 report

implementation_statement: SaaS vendors patch their applications. Automatic updates are on for the laptop and phone. Gap: the home router runs firmware from 2021 and has no update routine. Owner updates the router or replaces it by 2026-09-30 and checks firmware every quarter.

The laptop's built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning of downloads and attachments, a scheduled weekly scan, and automatic updates. The email provider scans attachments. The phone uses the platform's built-in protections and official app store only.
evidence: Antivirus status page; P07 test file

implementation_statement: No Section 889 check existed until the 2026-07-16 inquiry found the covered hotspot. POL-01 6.4 now requires checking the manufacturer of every network, phone, camera, or recording device against the FAR 52.204-25 list before purchase, and screening subcontractor submittals for FC-1 and the DoD subcontract.
evidence: Section 889 inquiry notes; report to the Contracting Officer 2026-07-17
